content.value_statement: 3D web projects can suffer from poor stack choices, slow assets, and weak fallbacks. This skill guides tool selection, scene implementation, optimization, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Recommends a 3D stack based on project goals, React usage, and control needs.
Shows React Three Fiber scene patterns with Canvas, controls, GLTF loading, and Suspense fallbacks.
Guides Spline embedding for quick 3D prototypes and visual scene delivery.
Explains model preparation, GLB or GLTF selection, compression, and mobile size targets.
Provides scroll-driven animation patterns using React Three Fiber and GSAP concepts.
Lists validation checks for loading states, WebGL fallbacks, DPR limits, and model optimization.
limitations: It does not create or optimize 3D asset files by itself.
It does not replace browser, device, or performance testing.
It assumes the project can use web 3D libraries or embedded Spline scenes.
It provides guidance and examples, not a complete production application.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Configurator
use_cases.description: Choose a 3D stack, prepare model assets, define variant interactions, and plan mobile fallbacks.

use_cases.title: Add 3D to a Portfolio
use_cases.description: Design an interactive scene, connect it to portfolio sections, and tune scroll-driven motion.

use_cases.title: Improve WebGL Performance
use_cases.description: Review model size, device pixel ratio, loading states, and fallback behavior for slower devices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a 3D Stack
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first 3D web project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Spline, React Three Fiber, Three.js, and Babylon.js for my project. Ask about framework, interaction depth, performance needs, and timeline before recommending a stack.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scene Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate project planning for a website section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 3D scene plan for a web page. Include the main object, camera behavior, lighting, loading state, fallback image, and mobile performance limits.

prompt_templates.title: Review a 3D Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing frontend build.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my 3D web implementation for performance and usability risks. Focus on model size, DPR settings, loading indicators, WebGL fallback, scroll handling, and accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Product Configurator
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product configurator as a 3D web architect. Propose improvements for asset compression, state management, color variants, mobile interaction, analytics events, and graceful fallback behavior.

output_examples.input: I need a 3D product viewer for a React storefront.
output: Recommended stack: React Three Fiber with GLB assets for deeper control inside React.
Core plan: load the model with a visible progress state, add color variant controls, and limit mobile DPR.
Fallback: provide a static product image when WebGL is unavailable or the device is underpowered.

output_examples.input: My 3D landing page feels slow on phones.
output: Likely causes include high triangle count, large textures, excessive lights, and high device pixel ratio.
Recommended fixes include GLB compression, WebP textures, one main directional light, and mobile DPR capped at 1.
Validation should include real device testing and a non-WebGL fallback path.

output_examples.input: I want scroll-based 3D motion for a portfolio.
output: Use scroll progress to drive camera movement or object rotation, with short scenes tied to content sections.
Avoid blocking normal page scroll with controls unless the interaction clearly needs it.
Add a reduced-motion experience and a static fallback for unsupported devices.

best_practices: Start with the simplest 3D stack that meets the interaction and control requirements.
Compress models and textures before tuning application code.
Always provide loading states, mobile limits, and non-WebGL fallbacks.
anti_patterns: Using full 3D scenes when a static image or short animation would serve the user better.
Shipping uncompressed models or high-resolution textures without device testing.
Letting camera controls or scroll effects block normal page navigation.

faq.question: What 3D libraries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Three.js, React Three Fiber, Spline, WebGL concepts, and related optimization patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with product configurators?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide stack choice, model loading, variant controls, mobile limits, and fallback planning.

faq.question: Does it create 3D models?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare and integrate models, but it does not create model assets.

faq.question: Does it support non-React projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses vanilla Three.js and Spline, but React Three Fiber examples are a major focus.

faq.question: How does it handle performance?
faq.answer: It recommends model compression, lower mobile DPR, limited lights, loading indicators, and fallbacks.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
